notes: Manuscript page number 47 is visible above the first baseline. Bottom-left pencil foliation reads 95, with its hand attribution left open. No date is written.

The opening concerns sets named A-tilde(G) and I(G), both with an application to S(G). The above-line origine names that application. Its curved attachment stroke is not an underline or an extra word.

The author introduces graphes avec branches aplaties and states a description using compact X and finite S: X is an étoile near every point of S, and each connected component of X minus S is a noncompact one-dimensional manifold with boundary. The parenthetical explanation says the quoted arête should have a vertex. The restatement calls X a topological 1-complex, requires S to contain vertices of order at least 3, and excludes compact connected components of X minus S. The text also states an equivalent condition using a map from S to a component symbol with index 0. These claims are reported, not independently proved or checked.

The final paragraph begins a combinatorial description by finite sets, an involution and an origin map. Several decorated set names remain unresolved. The sheet ends after une; its final grammatical construction is incomplete here.
Only one a-like word occurs before utiliser. It is retained as a/à without supplying C’s second word or H’s v. The opening reads et autre, with no added l-prime.

The 4-like glyph before couples is not asserted as a clean live numeral or an established cancellation. Its transverse stroke may belong to the glyph or a strike; alternatives preserve both possibilities. Inventory kind text is used because an independent deletion state is not demonstrated.

The cancellation crosses adhérence and following d-prime, stopping before the left quotation ticks of the live arête. The preceding word is tout without final e. Written grammar is retained. The covered adhérence remains doubtful.
The exact restatement word is compacte; H’s longer composante connexe de X is not substituted. Literal ∀ and = and both tt abbreviations are retained; expansions are confined to their list.

The component glyph is nearly cap-height with two downstrokes and a bowed right foot. Pi is the first candidate, while pi remains possible; conventional notation for components does not force the reading. This map and the final map each have a short downturned endpoint without a secure full arrowhead.

The three barred A/I loci are not interpreted as certified corrections of I into A. An additional tilde under a hat is not securely separable from retracing. Their collation rows describe unresolved differences, not established H errors. Clear tildes are retained at the tuple o index, object after involution de, final o index and final source. The later sigma index has its own tilde/hat doubt; no uniform accent is imposed.

The cancelled formula after où has initial decorated-A and lower A-like traces, but its relation and central character are crossed out. The retained equality/sigma expression is only the doubtful C candidate, not a certain recovered identity or a mathematical claim used here.

The original and both native halves were read line by line. Nine crops were created once at recorded original coordinates using LANCZOS enlargement, autocontrast and mild sharpening, with no rotation; all nine were inspected. The existing parenthesis crop was re-viewed to separate quotation ticks from cancellation and accent; no crop was regenerated. No OCR, outside research, TeX compilation or mathematical proof check was performed.

Main-reader accounting: rows C23–C26, C28, C30 and C33 are unresolved refinements of letter, accent or connector certainty. They remain in the supporting decisions/doubts record but are excluded from substantive C/H correction counts. In particular H’s double-accent forms are not classified as established errors, and the short terminal flicks do not certify a unique arrow class.

Blind audit reads the opening donnée with its two small terminal e bodies, preserving the literal ending. It broadens the a/à/va group, the identity/live-or-cancelled alternatives of the 4/q-like glyph, the tiny au/en pair, the cancelled et/a, the ornate Il/Ça, and the cancelled final formula. The retraced A/I forms and final one-sided endpoints remain unresolved; no correction history is asserted. H's va is now a permitted alternative, so that row is no longer counted as a settled textual difference against H.
